title: Silent Upstream Workarounds
pattern: Workarounds for external bugs written inline without tracking links, issue numbers, or alternative fallback plans.
why_bad: Fossils. When the upstream library fixes its bug, this workaround becomes an active bug. Without a tracked reference or automated test checking the upstream behavior, there is no trigger to clean it up.
detection: Inline comments mentioning third-party, upstream, or hardware library bugs without an accompanying link to an issue tracker or automated assertion checking for the bug.
counterexample: A workaround annotated with the upstream issue ID and guarded by an assertion or test that fails once the upstream bug is fixed.
fix: Add a tracking ID (e.g., ticket number, GitHub issue link) and wrap the workaround in a conditional runtime check or assertion.
source: Steve McConnell, *Code Complete* (2004), Chapter 32 ("Differentiate between major and minor comments - Code that works around an error").
